sections.html:
Think of this office as the county's memory for land: every deed, mortgage and other charge on a Jefferson County parcel ends up in its permanent record. The office is at 301 Market Street, Steubenville, OH 43952, and keeps weekday hours of 8:30 am to 4:30 pm. Request the current fee schedule when you phone. The staff is small, so send complete packets and call ahead.

All land in the county is recorded in this one place, from lots in Steubenville and Toronto to farms in the townships. Property across the river in Brooke or Hancock County, West Virginia, falls under West Virginia's own recording system.

sections.h2: What goes into a recording fee
sections.html:
R.C. 317.32 sets each recording charge as two equal halves: a base fee for the recorder and a matching fee for the Ohio housing trust fund. Get the Recorder's total for your paper before you write a check.

Statutory recording charges, each paid twice (recorder and trust fund)
ServiceEach of the two fees
Pages one and twoSeventeen dollars
Each added legal-size page or partial pageFour dollars
Marginal reference made by separate instrumentTwo dollars
Certified copy, per pageOne dollar, plus fifty cents for the seal

Senate Bill 94, effective October 24, 2024, let counties tack on a preservation surcharge of up to five dollars, kept in the general fund. Whether Jefferson County does so, and for how much, is a question for the Recorder.

The Auditor's counter collects in two layers. First comes the Auditor's fee under R.C. 319.54(G)(3): ten cents per hundred dollars of value, fractions counted, with a one dollar floor. On top of that, R.C. 322.02 lets a county adopt a transfer tax, capped at thirty cents per hundred dollars.

The county's 2025 annual financial report refers to a four mill permissive conveyance fee, with one of those mills dedicated to the GIS Fund by the commissioners. The Auditor is at 301 Market Street, P.O. Box 159, Steubenville, with phone (740) 283-8511 and fax (740) 283-8520. Call that office to confirm the rate, since a permissive levy is set by commissioner resolution.

Under R.C. 319.202(D) the seller pays. A transfer that qualifies as exempt carries a written statement of the reason in place of the fee.

sections.h2: Family transfers that skip the conveyance fee
sections.html:
The statute lists about two dozen exemptions. These are the ones families use most:

  • a gift from one spouse to the other, or from a parent to a child or the child's spouse
  • a deed passing between heirs or devisees of one decedent, as long as no money is paid
  • a deed placing the house in a trust the maker can cancel at will
  • a corrective or confirming deed that repairs one already of record
  • an interest worth one hundred dollars or less
  • a court-ordered transfer, unless it follows a sale under that order

Selling to an outside buyer is different. Even a quick as-is cash sale is a fee-paying transfer.

sections.h2: Order of steps: Auditor, then Recorder
sections.html:
The Auditor is first in line. If the county levies a transfer tax, the grantor owes it, paid to the auditor when the deed is delivered and before it is shown to the recorder (R.C. 322.02). The Auditor notes the fee amount on the deed, and the deed then goes to the Recorder.

A Steubenville title company can file a closing package electronically instead of carrying it across the floor, since Ohio recorders, auditors and engineers must provide electronic recording of conveyance papers (R.C. 317.13). If you are handling the deed yourself, carry the signed, notarized original in case the office wants paper.

sections.h2: What the Recorder does with your deed
sections.html:
Once the deed arrives with the Auditor's mark on it, the Recorder checks that it can be filed, enters it in the permanent record and returns it. After that the public record names the owner of the parcel. Before it, a buyer's claim is weaker than it looks, so closing agents do not let a signed deed sit on a desk.

The same counter handles the other papers that tie to your parcel. The buyer's new mortgage is recorded here, and so is the release that clears your old loan. Easements and leases go through the same office. A stray lien or an old mortgage nobody ever released can slow a closing by days, so raise it with your title company before you list.

sections.h2: Selling for cash in Jefferson County
sections.html:
A cash buyer has no lender's appraisal or underwriting to wait on, so the courthouse side is a short chain: deed, Auditor, Recorder. The fees stay the same, though. Recording charges and the conveyance fee come due on a cash sale just as on a financed one, and you pay the conveyance fee at closing.

A house that needs work or has an unpaid tax bill calls for an early payoff figure from the title company. Amounts owed on the parcel come out of your proceeds, and the title company cannot promise a closing date without them. Heirs selling an inherited house should read the exemption list above first, since a deed between heirs with no money changing hands may owe nothing.

Jefferson County had 63,597 residents and 30,964 housing units in 2025, and owners occupy 70.5% of homes. The typical owner-occupied home sells near a $127,800 value, monthly gross rent is $835 and household income is $59,055. The county's population has slid 2.5% since the 2020 base, so expect a buyer pool that leans local. Many residents work in the Weirton-Steubenville metropolitan area, which adds Brooke and Hancock counties in West Virginia. Buyers who commute across the river may be shopping in both states, so be ready to explain Ohio's process if an out-of-state agent calls. Pricing near the river towns often moves with job news from the Steubenville area, and a clean deed with clear paperwork keeps a sale on schedule when a buyer is on a deadline.

sections.h2: Before you take the deed in
sections.html:
Pull these together first: the signed, notarized deed, the parcel number and the full legal description. Phone the Auditor about the conveyance fee and the permissive fee. Phone the Recorder for the total on your page count, including any preservation surcharge. An exempt transfer needs its exemption statement stapled to the deed.

Your lender files its own release when the mortgage is paid off, and your title company can confirm it reached the Recorder. File the Auditor's marked copy with the recorded deed.

faqs.q: Which office records the deed on a house in Steubenville?
faqs.a: The Jefferson County Recorder at 301 Market Street. Steubenville is inside Jefferson County, so deeds there are filed in that office.

faqs.q: Does Jefferson County charge the optional document preservation surcharge?
faqs.a: Ask the Recorder. State law lets a county add up to five dollars, and the office can say what, if anything, it adds to a deed.

faqs.q: Who pays the conveyance fee on a Jefferson County sale?
faqs.a: The seller does. As grantor, you owe the Auditor's fee and any Chapter 322 transfer tax the county levies (R.C. 319.202(D)).

faqs.q: Does a gift of a house from a parent to a child owe the conveyance fee?
faqs.a: No, subdivision (d) of R.C. 319.54(G)(3) exempts it. The deed still goes to the Auditor with an exemption statement before it is recorded.

faqs.q: What is the four mill fee in the Jefferson County financial report?
faqs.a: It is the county's permissive conveyance fee. The commissioners dedicated one mill of it to the county's GIS Fund, which keeps the parcel maps current.
